_note: Agronomic profiles per crop. Compiled from public Bangladesh sources (BRRI, BARC FRG-2018, DAE crop calendars, FAO). Soil scores are 0-1 suitability. Stages use DAS = days after sowing/transplanting (negative = before).

T. Aman Rice.water_note: mostly rainfed in Kharif-2; supplemental irrigation if monsoon breaks
T. Aman Rice.risk_note: flood/submergence risk in low-lying land; stem borer, BLB
T. Aman Rice.source: BRRI Adhunik Dhaner Chash; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Plough 2-3 times, puddle, level; incorporate cowdung 2 t/acre
Transplant 25-30 day seedlings, 2-3 per hill, 20x15 cm spacing
Apply full TSP, MoP and gypsum at final land preparation
1/3 urea after seedling establishment
Hand weeding or rotary weeder
1/3 urea at active tillering
Scout for stem borer dead-hearts and leaf folder; perching
1/3 urea at panicle initiation
Watch BLB/blast at booting; avoid excess N
Drain 10-15 days before harvest
Harvest at 80% golden grain; dry to 14% moisture

Boro Rice.water_note: fully irrigated crop; needs reliable water ~1000-1200 mm equivalent
Boro Rice.risk_note: irrigation cost, cold injury at seedling, hailstorm at harvest
Boro Rice.source: BRRI Adhunik Dhaner Chash; BARC FRG-2018

stages.action: Puddle and level; ensure irrigation channel
Transplant 35-40 day seedlings (older for cold)
Full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc at final prep
1/3 urea; keep 2-3 cm standing water
Weed before second top-dress
1/3 urea at maximum tillering
Stem borer, BPH scouting at base of hills
1/3 urea at panicle initiation
No water stress from booting to grain fill
Drain before harvest
Harvest April-May before pre-monsoon hail

Maize (Kharif).water_note: sensitive to waterlogging; ensure drainage in monsoon
Maize (Kharif).risk_note: fall armyworm scouting needed; otherwise hardy
Maize (Kharif).source: DAE maize production guide; BARC FRG-2018

stages.action: 2-3 ploughings; make drainage furrows
60x20 cm spacing, 1 seed/hill, 8-9 kg/acre hybrid seed
1/3 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc
Thin to one plant/hill; first weeding
1/3 urea at knee-high (V8), earth up
Fall armyworm scouting in whorls; hand-pick egg masses
1/3 urea before tasseling
No stress at tasseling-silking if dry spell
Harvest when husks dry and black layer forms

Potato.risk_note: late blight in foggy weather; price crash risk at peak harvest
Potato.source: BARI potato guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Fine tilth; ridges 60 cm apart; cowdung 4 t/acre
Whole/cut seed tubers 25 cm apart on ridges
1/2 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc, boron
Light irrigation at stolon initiation
Remaining 1/2 urea; earth up ridges
Late blight watch when night fog + 10-20°C; prophylactic mancozeb
Tuber bulking irrigations; stop 10 days pre-harvest
Cut haulms to harden skin
Harvest, cure in shade, grade before storage

Wheat.water_note: 2-3 irrigations: CRI (20-25 DAS), booting, grain fill
Wheat.risk_note: late sowing after Dec 15 cuts yield ~1%/day; blast in warm humid Feb

stages.action: 2-3 ploughings with residual moisture
Line sowing 20 cm rows, 48-50 kg/acre seed
2/3 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, boron
Crown root initiation irrigation — most critical
Remaining 1/3 urea right after CRI irrigation
One hand weeding
Booting stage irrigation
Wheat blast watch if Feb is warm and humid
Grain filling irrigation
Harvest mid-March before heat stress

Mustard.water_note: 0-2 light irrigations; fits between Aman harvest and Boro
Mustard.risk_note: aphids in cool cloudy weather; short duration limits exposure
Mustard.source: BARI mustard guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Fine tilth on residual moisture after Aman
Broadcast/line sow 3 kg/acre (BARI Sarisha-14/17)
1/2 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, boron, zinc
Thin to 5 cm plant spacing
Remaining 1/2 urea before flowering, with irrigation if dry
Aphid colonies on inflorescence; spray only past threshold
One light irrigation at siliqua fill if dry
Harvest when 75-80% siliquae turn straw colour

Jute.water_note: pre-monsoon showers for establishment; retting water at harvest
Jute.risk_note: price volatility; retting water scarcity; hairy caterpillar
Jute.source: BJRI jute guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Fine tilth; 2-3 ploughings
Line sow 2.5-3 kg/acre (O-9897 / Robi-1)
1/2 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum
Thin to 7-8 cm; first weeding
Remaining 1/2 urea after weeding
Hairy caterpillar — collect egg-mass leaves
Cut at small pod stage for best fibre
Ret in clean slow water 12-15 days; strip and dry

Aus Rice.water_note: pre-monsoon showers for establishment, then early monsoon; some risk of early drought
Aus Rice.risk_note: drought at establishment then flash flood; lower yield than Aman/Boro
Aus Rice.source: BRRI Adhunik Dhaner Chash; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Dry ploughing 2-3 times before pre-monsoon showers
Direct broadcast/line sow 12-15 kg/acre (BRRI dhan48/98)
1/3 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum
First weeding; thin dense patches
1/3 urea at tillering
Second weeding before top-dress
1/3 urea at panicle initiation
Stem borer and rice bug scouting
Harvest Jul-Aug at 80% ripening before monsoon flood

Lentil.water_note: grows on residual moisture; 0-1 irrigation; a very low-cost Rabi pulse
Lentil.risk_note: stemphylium blight in humid cloudy spells; aphids; low cash cost overall
Lentil.source: BARI lentil (masur) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Fine tilth on residual moisture after Aman
Broadcast/line sow 15 kg/acre (BARI Masur-6/8)
Full urea (light), TSP, MoP, gypsum, boron at sowing
One weeding at branching
Stemphylium blight watch in fog; spray mancozeb if needed
One light irrigation at flowering if soil very dry
Aphid scouting at podding
Harvest when 80% pods turn brown

sowing_window.label: sow late Oct to late Nov

Chickpea.water_note: deep-rooted, drought-tolerant; usually rainfed on residual moisture
Chickpea.risk_note: pod borer (Helicoverpa); botrytis grey mould and wilt in wet years
Chickpea.source: BARI chickpea (chola) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Coarse tilth on residual moisture; do not over-pulverize
Line sow 12-14 kg/acre (BARI Chola-5/9/10)
Light urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, boron at sowing
One weeding at early branching
Botrytis grey mould watch in cloudy humid spells
Pod borer — pheromone traps, spray at flowering/podding if past threshold
Harvest when plants yellow and pods dry

sowing_window.label: sow mid-Feb to end-Mar (also after Aman)

Mungbean.water_note: very short duration; fits fallow gaps; 1-2 irrigations in dry spells
Mungbean.risk_note: yellow mosaic virus (whitefly-spread) and thrips; short exposure limits losses
Mungbean.source: BARI mungbean (mug) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Single fine tilth; quick turnaround crop
Line sow 5-6 kg/acre (BARI Mug-6/8)
Light urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum at sowing
One weeding at branching
Whitefly (yellow mosaic) and thrips scouting
First pick of mature dry pods
Second/final pick when pods blacken

Onion.water_note: shallow-rooted; needs frequent light irrigation; stop before harvest
Onion.risk_note: purple blotch, thrips, and severe post-harvest price volatility/storage rot
Onion.source: BARI onion (peyaj) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Fine tilth; raised beds; cowdung 4 t/acre
Transplant 40-45 day seedlings 10x10 cm (BARI Peyaj-1/4)
1/2 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc, boron
First weeding; keep beds clean
Remaining 1/2 urea at bulb initiation
Thrips and purple blotch — spray if past threshold
Light irrigation every 8-10 days during bulbing
Stop watering to harden bulbs
Harvest when 50-70% tops fall; cure in shade before storage

sowing_window.label: plant late Oct to late Nov

Garlic.water_note: steady moisture; can be grown zero-till (dibbled) after Aman on soft soil
Garlic.risk_note: expensive seed cloves dominate cost; storage loss; leaf blight
Garlic.source: BARI garlic (rosun) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Fine tilth or zero-till dibbling on soft moist soil
Dibble healthy cloves 10x10 cm, tip up (BARI Rosun-1/3/4)
1/2 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc, boron
Straw mulch to conserve moisture and suppress weeds
Hand weeding; avoid damaging shallow roots
Remaining 1/2 urea at bulbing
Light irrigation every 10-12 days during bulb growth
Leaf blight/purple blotch watch in humid spells
Stop watering to mature bulbs
Harvest when tops dry; cure and bundle for storage

Chili.water_note: sensitive to waterlogging; needs drainage; steady moisture at fruiting
Chili.risk_note: anthracnose fruit rot, thrips/mite leaf-curl, and sharp price swings
Chili.source: BARI chili (morich) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Raise seedlings in raised beds 30-35 days before transplant
Fine tilth; ridges/beds with good drainage
Transplant seedlings 50x40 cm (BARI Morich-1/3)
1/3 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc, boron
First weeding and earthing up
1/3 urea at vegetative growth
Thrips/mite (leaf curl) — spray if leaves cup/curl
1/3 urea at flowering
Anthracnose fruit rot watch in wet weather; spray as needed
First pick of mature green/red fruit
Multiple pickings; dry red chili if selling dry

Tomato.water_note: needs staking and drainage; steady moisture; avoid waterlogging
Tomato.risk_note: late blight, whitefly-borne leaf curl virus (TYLCV), fruit borer; peak-season price crash
Tomato.source: BARI tomato guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Raise seedlings 28-30 days before transplant
Fine tilth; ridges; cowdung 4 t/acre
Transplant 60x40 cm (BARI Tomato-14/15 or hybrids)
1/2 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc, boron
Stake plants; begin tying
Whitefly (leaf curl) and fruit borer — pheromone traps
Remaining 1/2 urea in 2 splits from flowering
Late blight watch in fog; prophylactic mancozeb
First pick at breaker stage
Multiple pickings; sell staggered to avoid glut price

Brinjal.water_note: long harvest window; steady moisture; grows in both winter and monsoon
Brinjal.risk_note: brinjal shoot & fruit borer (major), bacterial wilt; heavy pesticide unless IPM/Bt
Brinjal.source: BARI brinjal (begun) guide; DAE IPM leaflet

stages.action: Raise seedlings 35-40 days before transplant
Fine tilth; ridges; cowdung 4 t/acre
Transplant 75x60 cm (BARI Begun varieties)
1/3 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc, boron
First weeding and earthing up
Shoot & fruit borer — pheromone traps, clip infested shoots weekly
Remaining urea in splits through the harvest period
First pick of glossy tender fruit
Pick every 4-5 days over a long season

Groundnut.water_note: loves light sandy/char soils; needs gypsum and moisture at pegging/pod fill
Groundnut.risk_note: tikka leaf spot; needs calcium (gypsum) for pod fill; low risk on drained sandy land
Groundnut.source: BARI groundnut (chinabadam) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Loose fine tilth (light soils ideal)
Line sow 40-48 kg/acre in-shell (BARI Chinabadam-8/9)
Low urea + full TSP, MoP, half gypsum at sowing
Weed and loosen soil for peg entry
Remaining gypsum at pegging for pod fill (calcium)
Tikka leaf spot watch; spray if spotting spreads
Irrigation at pegging and pod fill if dry
Harvest when inner shell veins darken; dry pods well

Sugarcane.water_note: long-duration; needs many irrigations in the dry months; ties up land ~11 months
Sugarcane.risk_note: long land occupation, stem/top borer, mill payment delays; low margin per month
Sugarcane.source: BSRI sugarcane (aakh) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Deep ploughing; open furrows 90-120 cm apart
Plant 3-budded setts end to end in furrows (BSRI Ganda varieties)
1/3 urea + full TSP, MoP, gypsum, zinc in furrow
Fill gaps to keep full stand
First weeding at tillering
1/3 urea and earthing up
Second weeding
Final 1/3 urea before grand growth
Stem/top borer — remove dead-hearts, release Trichogramma
Tie canes to prevent lodging in storms
Harvest at maturity; deliver to mill/gur promptly

Sweet Potato.water_note: thrives on light sandy/char soils; drought-tolerant; minimal irrigation
Sweet Potato.risk_note: sweet potato weevil in dry cracked soil; otherwise very hardy and cheap
Sweet Potato.source: BARI sweet potato (mishti alu) guide; DAE crop calendar

stages.action: Make ridges/mounds 60 cm apart on loose soil
Plant 25-30 cm vine cuttings on ridges (BARI Mishti Alu varieties)
1/2 urea + full TSP, MoP at planting
Replace failed cuttings
Weed and lift vines to stop rooting at nodes
Remaining 1/2 urea and earthing up
Weevil — keep ridges earthed; avoid soil cracks
Harvest when leaves yellow; cure roots before storage
